text:
Colorado arrives with a 6-3 win over Tampa Bay on Friday that ended the Lightning's three-game winning streak, though the Avalanche are 2-2-1 in their last five and are without Nicolas Roy and Zachary L'Heureux. Nashville is on the second night of a back-to-back after losing 3-2 in overtime in Pittsburgh, and is 1-2-2 over its last five, outscored 19-11. There is some reunion flavor: Jack Drury and Ross Colton face the Avalanche for the first time since leaving them, and Fedor Svechkov is back in Nashville.

COL has been the better team at five on five, taking 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) against 43% for NSH. The Avalanche also create more per 60 minutes (3.34 to 2.83) and give up fewer (2.8 to 3.29). Special teams are close, but COL's power play generates 0.68 expected goals a game to NSH's 0.57. In net, projected starters Mackenzie Blackwood and Justus Annunen are both below expected this season (-1.05 and -1.52 goals saved above expected), though each was about seven goals better than expected last year. Annunen starts over Juuse Saros.

Nathan MacKinnon is 44% to score and 87% for a point. Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette posted that the first goal Thursday was a "vintage Avalanche rush." Among our under-the-radar picks, T.J. Hughes has produced 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games on the third line, and we have him at 21% to score. Nazem Kadri is 58% for a point.
